name: Rest reset at constant temperature 6 h
description: Decides whether the one-way UL transient is reset by REST ALONE, at unchanged temperature. Background: on 20260924_065556 UL fell -29 to -53 % during the first hours and did not recover when the oil was cooled back to the same 41 C. But measuring the same window on two consecutive days showed it HAD recovered overnight: at identical 41 C, 2026-09-24 started +56 to +93 % above 2026-09-23. A bushing that seats stays seated and a clamp that settles stays settled, so the transient is not those -- it is something reset by standing still. Two candidates remain: the OIL FILM redistributing while the rig rests, and a THERMO-MECHANICAL state that resets on cooling. The overnight recovery cannot separate them, because the rig also cooled to 25 C. This profile removes temperature from the experiment entirely: SV is held at 40 C from the first second to the last, so nothing thermal changes at any point. The same measurement block (1500/2000/2500/3000 rpm, 5 min each, then 5 min at rest) is taken four times: A after the overnight stand, B after 2 h of running so the transient is spent, C after the shaft has STOOD STILL FOR AN HOUR at the same 40 C, and D after a further hour of running. READ IT LIKE THIS: if C jumps back up toward A while the temperature never moved, rest alone resets the transient and the cause is the oil film, not a thermal state. If C stays down at B's level, rest at constant temperature does NOT reset it, and the overnight recovery was thermal after all. D then says whether it falls again on the second running stretch, i.e. whether the cycle repeats. The hour of rest is the whole point of the run; do not shorten it. Effective stand is ~65 min because block B already ends with 5 min at rest. Same acquisition and scope_channels as Keratech22 and UL_TempCycle_6h, so all three compare directly.
